REQUIREMENTS FOR PACKING OF PESTICIDES
`PART 2 LIQUID PESTICIDES (

Second Revision )
0 . FOREWORL)

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 2 ) ( Second Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 3 October 1988, after the draft finalized by the Packaging of Chemicals Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging Division Council.

Since the packing requirements covered in this standald have been adopted by the Registration Committee constituted under the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968, this standard assumes statutory character. 0.3 The list of Indian Standards relating to packaging referred to in this standard is given in Appendix A. 0.4 This standard has been pubiished in four parts. This part ( Part 2 ) covers the requirements for packing of liquid pesticide?. The other parts are: Part : Solid Pesticidei Part 3 Household Pesticides Part 4 Fumigants 42BA or 42BB having melt flow index ( is ) not more than 1.8 g/l0 min ( see IS : 7328-1974 ). 2.4 Aluminium used in the fabrication of containers ( see IS : 9503-1980 ) shall conform to Grade 19 500 of IS : 737-1974.. 2.5 Containers of mild steel and tinplate shall also be painted/lacquered externally to prevent rusting from outside, if not lithographed. If lithographed, top and bottom components shall be lacquered externally. 2.6 Closures provided shall be such as not to allow any material to leak through them. These shall be tamperproof. 2.7 Containers holding 5 litres or more o-f liquid pesticides shall be provided with a suitable pouring device with each container. 2.8 The packing shall also conform to the tariff rules in force from time to time for the packing
*Specification for wrought aluminium and aluminium alloy sheet and strip for general engineering purpores ( second revision ) .

0.2 This standard, issued in 1976, was first revised in 1980. This second revision has been undertaken to incorporate the packing requirements for pesticides as modified through various a m e n d m e n t s i s s u e d ~subsequently and a!s? to include packing requirements for some pestlcldes for which the related Indian Standard Specifications have been published in the meanwhile. For some pesticides, technical and their formulations, the packing requirements have been suitably changed wherever new/alternative packing materials have been approved. I. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 2 ) covers the requirements for packing of liquid pesticides. 1.2 This standard does not cover the packing requirements for liquid pesticides meant f o r household use and fumigants. 2. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 2.1 The liquid pesticides, technical and their formulations, exce t otherwise specified in Tables 1 to 3 shall be patE ed in containers in the quantities of 100 ml, 250 ml, 500 ml, 1 1, 5 1, 10 1, 20 I, 25 1 and 50 1. Technical grade and emulsifiable concentrates meant for bulk consumpti6n may also be packed in quantities of 200 litres in a container. 2.2 Retail packs up to 1 litre shall be further packed in corrugated fibreboard boxes [ see IS : 2771 ( Part i )-1977 ] or wooden cases ( see IS : 1503-1979 ) when they require transportation. 2.3 The high density polyethylene ( HDPE ) used in the fabrication of ,HDPE container or its components shall be of designation HDPE 43BA, 1

IS : 8190 ( Part 2 ) - 1988 of goods falling in the category of materials of low flash point, dangerous and toxic, wherever applicable. ~2.9 The cbntainers shall be of sturdy design and shall confbrm to the relevant IndianStandards. 3. SPECIFIC 3.1 Technical REQUIREMENTS Grade Pesticides - The technical grade pesticides shall -be pakked in dry and clean containers as described in Table 1. 3.2 Emulmifiabk Concentrates - The emulrifiable concentrates shall be packed in dry and clean containers as described in Table 2. Formulations - The 3.3 O t h e r L i q u i d following liquid formulations shall be packed in clean and dry containers as described in Table 3.
